Chapter 11: The Gifts of Imperfection—Letting Go of What We’re Supposed to Be.
Have you ever noticed how much energy you spend trying to look perfect, act perfect, or just... be perfect? There’s this quiet freedom that shows up when you finally let that go. Most people don’t even realize just how exhausting it is, chasing those impossible standards—whether it’s at work, at home, or even in our closest relationships.
Think about a student, juggling classes and activities, feeling like she has to be the best at everything. The pressure builds until it’s just too much, and suddenly, she breaks down in tears. But in that moment, something shifts. She realizes—she doesn’t have to do it all or do it perfectly. She doesn’t have to carry everything on her own.
Letting go of perfection isn’t about giving up or saying you don’t care. It’s about recognizing that being human means being messy, making mistakes, and still being worthy of love and belonging.
Picture a parent who, after a rough day, snaps at his child. The guilt sets in, but instead of pretending nothing happened, he apologizes. He asks for forgiveness. It’s awkward, sure, but it actually brings them closer together.
We all fall into the trap of comparing ourselves to others, thinking everyone else has it all figured out. But the truth? Everyone struggles. Everyone falls short sometimes. When you let go of what you think you’re supposed to be, you finally get the chance to accept who you really are.
Imagine a manager who flubs a big presentation. Instead of hiding her mistakes, she opens up to her team, shares what she learned, and invites their feedback. The team steps up with support, and together, they find new ways to move forward.
Here’s the real gift in all of this: when you let go of the need to be perfect, you open yourself up to freedom, connection, creativity, and joy. You get to live more fully, love more deeply, and bounce back from setbacks even stronger than before.
